economy.summary: His campaign says he will fight to lower the cost of living, addressing housing, rent, and healthcare costs and supporting small businesses; he proposes removing sales taxes on home maintenance items.
economy.short: Proposes lowering living costs; supports small businesses.

taxes.summary: Proposes limiting property tax increases to the rate of inflation, lowering the Allegheny County sales tax to match neighboring counties, and auditing state welfare programs to prevent fraud.
taxes.short: Proposes capping property tax increases, lowering county sales tax.

education.summary: Supports school choice through voucher programs, parental rights, curriculum transparency, and expanded vocational training; his platform also includes barring transgender students from girls' school sports.
education.short: Supports school choice vouchers, parental rights, curriculum transparency.

healthcare.summary: His campaign says he will work to lower healthcare costs and expand insurance options for small-business employees; the site does not detail a broader healthcare plan.
healthcare.short: Says he will lower healthcare costs, expand insurance options.

energy.summary: Supports expanding power generation, including nuclear, coal, natural gas, and solar, to bring prices down, and proposes requiring data centers to provide their own power rather than drawing on community supply.
energy.short: Supports expanding nuclear, coal, gas, solar power generation.

guns.summary: Supports expanding the right to keep and bear arms, including stand-your-ground laws, permitless carry, and nationwide reciprocity; on public safety he supports law enforcement, expanded mandatory minimum sentences, and ending cashless bail.
guns.short: Supports permitless carry, stand-your-ground; backs law enforcement.

economy.summary: Her campaign platform says a healthy economy should reward hard work and provide opportunity for families, small businesses, and workers, and supports job growth, workforce development, and responsible fiscal policies to keep the region affordable and competitive.
economy.short: Supports job growth, workforce development, responsible fiscal policies.

abortion.summary: As the incumbent, voted yes in December 2025 on House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment that would add reproductive-rights protections to the Pennsylvania Constitution; the bill passed the House and went to the Senate.
abortion.short: Voted yes on state constitutional reproductive-rights amendment.

education.summary: Her platform says every child in the district deserves access to a high-quality public education and supports strong school funding, workforce training programs, affordable higher-education pathways, and school safety initiatives.
education.short: Supports public school funding, workforce training, school safety.

healthcare.summary: As the incumbent, sponsored a bill requiring private insurance to cover at-home blood pressure monitors for postpartum mothers, part of the Black Maternal Health Caucus's 'Momnibus 2.0' package; it passed the House in June 2025.
healthcare.short: Sponsored bill requiring insurance cover postpartum blood-pressure monitors.

energy.summary: Her platform supports expanding clean and reliable energy options, transition support for workers, and protecting air and water resources, saying the region can stay competitive and create good-paying jobs through clean energy.
energy.short: Supports expanding clean energy, worker transitions, protecting air, water.

guns.summary: Her platform says the right to own firearms is protected and supports background checks, waiting periods, and modernized hunting laws including Sunday hunting; on public safety she supports community policing with mental health resources alongside law enforcement funding.
guns.short: Supports background checks, waiting periods; says gun ownership protected.
